questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses and Eleazar to do after the plague?
questions.a: Yahweh told them to count all the people of Israel from 20 years old and up, by their tribes, who were able to go to war.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh speak to after the plague ended?
questions.a: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest.

questions.q: Where were Moses and Eleazar when they spoke to the people of Israel?
questions.a: They were in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan River, across from Jericho.

questions.q: What did Moses and Eleazar tell the people Yahweh had commanded them to do?
questions.a: They told the people they needed to count the people from 20 years old and up, who had come out of the land of Egypt.

questions.q: Who was the firstborn of Israel?
questions.a: The firstborn of Israel was Reuben.

questions.q: What were the names of the last two clans descended from Reuben?
questions.a: They were the clan of Hezron and the clan of Carmi.

questions.q: How many men did the clans of Reuben’s descendants number?
questions.a: The clans of Reuben’s descendants numbered 43,730 men.

questions.q: Who was the son of Pallu?
questions.a: The son of Pallu was Eliab.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Eliab, descendant of Reuben, and what did his sons do?
questions.a: Eliab’s sons were Nemuel, Dathan and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram rebelled against Yahweh by following Korah who had challenged Moses and Aaron.

questions.q: What happened to all the followers of Korah that became a warning sign?
questions.a: The earth swallowed them up and fire devoured 250 men.

questions.q: Whose sons did not die?
questions.a: Korah’s sons did not die.

questions.q: What were the first three clans descended from Simeon?
questions.a: They were the clans of Nemuel, Jamin, and Jachin.

questions.q: What were the last two clans descended from Simeon?
questions.a: They were the clans of Zerah and Shaul.

questions.q: Who was listed next of Israel’s sons, and how many did their descendants number?
questions.a: The clans of Simeon were the next of Israel’s sons; they numbered 22,200 total men.

questions.q: What two clans of Gad’s descendants came after Shuni?
questions.a: They were the clans of Ozni and Eri.

questions.q: What were the first three clans descended from Gad?
questions.a: They were the clans of Zephon, Haggi, and Shuni.

questions.q: What were the last two clans descended from Gad?
questions.a: They were the clans of Arod and Areli.

questions.q: How many did the male descendants of Gad number?
questions.a: The male descendants of Gad numbered 40,500 men.

questions.q: What happened to Judah’s sons, Er and Onan?
questions.a: They died in the land of Canaan.

questions.q: Which sons of Judah had descendants who formed clans?
questions.a: Shelah, Perez, and Zerah had descendants who formed clans.

questions.q: What were the names of Perez’s two sons?
questions.a: They were Hezron and Hamul.

questions.q: How many men were in the other descendants of Judah?
questions.a: The other descendants of Judah numbered 76,500 men.

questions.q: What were the first two clans descended from Issachar?
questions.a: They were the clans of Tola and Puvah.

questions.q: What were the last two clans descended from Issachar?
questions.a: They were the clans of Jashub and Shimron.

questions.q: What was the number of the men of the clans from Issachar’s descendants?
questions.a: The number of the men of the clans from Issachar’s descendants was 64,300 men.

questions.q: What were the three clans descended from Zebulun?
questions.a: They were the clans of Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.

questions.q: What was the number of the men from Zebulun’s descendants?
questions.a: The number of the men from Zebulun’s descendants was 60,500 men.

questions.q: What were the two clans descended from Joseph?
questions.a: The two clans descended from Joseph were Manasseh and Ephraim.

questions.q: Who was Makir’s son?
questions.a: Makir’s son was Gilead.

questions.q: What were the first two clans descended from Gilead?
questions.a: They were the clans of Iezer and Helek.

questions.q: What two clans of Gilead’s descendants came after Helek?
questions.a: They were the clans of Asriel and Shechem.

questions.q: What were the last two clans descended from Gilead?
questions.a: They were the clans of Shemida and Hepher.

questions.q: How many daughters did Zelophehad son of Hepher have although he had no sons?
questions.a: Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons and had five daughters.

questions.q: How many men came from the descendants of Manasseh?
questions.a: The men that came from the descendants of Manasseh numbered 52,700 men.

questions.q: What were the three clans descended from Ephraim?
questions.a: They were the clans of Shuthelah, Becher, and Tahan.

questions.q: What clan descended from Shuthelah?
questions.a: The clan of Eran descended from Shuthelah.

questions.q: How many men came from the descendants of Ephraim?
questions.a: The men that came from the descendants of Ephraim numbered 32,500 men.

questions.q: What were the first three clans descended from Benjamin?
questions.a: They were the clans of Bela, Ashbel, and Ahiram.

questions.q: What were the last two clans descended from Benjamin?
questions.a: They were the clans of Shephupham and Hupham.

questions.q: What were the names of Bela’s two sons?
questions.a: They were Ard and Naaman.

questions.q: How many men came from the descendants of Benjamin?
questions.a: The men that came from the descendants of Benjamin numbered 45,600 men.

questions.q: What was the one clan descended from Dan?
questions.a: It was the clan of Shuham.

questions.q: How many men came from the descendants of Dan?
questions.a: The men that came from the descendants of Dan were numbered 64,400 men.

questions.q: What were the three clans descended from Asher?
questions.a: They were the clans of Imnah, Ishvi, and Beriah.

questions.q: What were the names of Beriah’s two sons?
questions.a: They were Heber and Malchiel.

questions.q: What was the name of Asher’s daughter?
questions.a: Her name was Serah.

questions.q: How many men came from the descendants of Asher?
questions.a: The men that came from the descendants of Asher numbered 53,400 men.

questions.q: What were the first two clans descended from Naphtali?
questions.a: They were the clans of Jahzeel and Guni.

questions.q: What were the last two clans descended from Naphtali?
questions.a: They were the clans of Jezer and Shillem.

questions.q: How many men were numbered from the descendants of Naphtali?
questions.a: The men that came from the descendants of Naphtali were numbered 45,400 men.

questions.q: What was the complete count of the men of the people of Israel?
questions.a: The complete count of men from among the people of Israel was 601,730.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh speak to about how the land would be divided?
questions.a: Yahweh spoke to Moses.

questions.q: How did Yahweh say the land would be divided?
questions.a: Yahweh said to divide the land among those men as an inheritance according to the number of their names.

questions.q: Who would get more and who would get less land for their inheritance?
questions.a: The clans who were larger in number would be given more inheritance and the clans who were smaller in number would be given less inheritance.

questions.q: What way would be used to divide the land?
questions.a: The land would be divided by lots, according to the tribes of their ancestors.

questions.q: From what clan were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari?
questions.a: Gershon, Kohath, and Marari were from the Levite clans.

questions.q: From what clan did the Libnites, Hebronites, Mahlites, Mushites, and Korahites descend?
questions.a: The Libnites, Hebronites, Mahlites, Mushites, and Korahites were descended from Levi.

questions.q: Who was Amram’s ancestor?
questions.a: Amram’s ancestor was Kohath.

questions.q: Who were the children of Amram and Jochebed, a descendant of Levi who was born in Egypt?
questions.a: Their children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam, their sister.

questions.q: Who was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar?
questions.a: Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

questions.q: What happened to Nadab and Abihu and why did they die?
questions.a: Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before Yahweh.

questions.q: What was the number of males from Levi that were one month old and older?
questions.a: The number of males from Levi who were one month old and older was 23,000.

questions.q: Why were the male Levites one month old and up not counted among the other people of Israel?
questions.a: The male Levites one month old and up were not counted among the other people of Israel because they were not given a land inheritance among the Israelites.

questions.q: Where did Moses and Eleazar the priest count the people of Israel?
questions.a: Moses and Eleazar counted the people of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.

questions.q: How many men were found who had been counted by Moses and Aaron the priest when the descendants of Israel had been counted in the wilderness of Sinai?
questions.a: None of the men whom Moses and Aaron the priest counted in the wilderness of Sinai were among these men.

questions.q: Why were Moses and Aaron not able to count these descendants again?
questions.a: Yahweh had said that those people would die in the wilderness, except for Caleb and Joshua.

commentary.text: Numbering of Israel in the plains of Moab.
None remaining of the first numbering.

Verses 1–51 Moses did not number the people but when God commanded him. We have here the families registered, as well as the tribes. The total was nearly the same as when numbered at mount Sinai. Notice is here taken of the children of Korah; they died not, as the children of Dathan and Abiram; they seem not to have joined even their own father in rebellion. If we partake not of the sins of sinners, we shall not partake of their plagues. (Nu 26:52-56)

In distributing these tribes, the general rule of equity is prescribed; that to many should be given more, and to fewer less. Though it seems left to the prudence of their prince, the matter at last must be settled by the providence of God, with which all must be satisfied.
Levi was God's tribe; therefore it was not numbered with the rest, but alone. It came not under the sentence, that none of them should enter Canaan excepting Caleb and Joshua.

The execution of the sentence passed on the murmurers, chap. 14:29, is observable. There was not one man numbered now, who was numbered then, but Caleb and Joshua. Here appeared the righteousness of God, and his faithfulness to his threatenings. Especially observe the truth of God, in performing his promise to Caleb and Joshua. Death makes awful havoc of the human species, and causes surprising changes in families and nations; yet all is appointed in perfect wisdom, justice, and truth, by the Lord himself. This should stir us up to think upon the hateful nature of sin, the cause of all these devastations. We should renew our repentance, seek forgiveness, value the salvation of Christ, remember how frail we are, prepare for the summons of death, and fill up our days in serving our generation according to the will of God.
